title: A World of Parallel Branches
paragraphs: “What do you mean, ‘how’?”
“It seems Father is afraid that because he eliminated the Crimson Swine, Trash and the others might come after him. But if you give the order, I’ll blow up the castle and the church for you.”
“There’s no way you could do that.”
You’re pretty suspicious, aren’t you? Well, wouldn’t it be best to actually show you my power?
“Then I’d like you to witness my strength firsthand.”
“Huh? I just saw it. A beam shoots out of your spear, right?”

A beam from a spear? Oh, you mean Brionac. That’s just a matter of special effects. I’ll demonstrate a proof of strength passed down directly from Father. Right… there’s a swamp a short distance away. Let’s target that area.

“I, The Love Hunter, command the heavens and the earth; I sever and reconnect the order of things, and force out the pus. O power of the Dragon Vein. Unite with my Magical Power and the hero’s might—The Love Hunter, the very source of power, commands: Decipher all things in the universe once more, and bring forth a false sun!”
“Liberation Prominence X!”

I’ll cast the Orb of flame created by the spell straight at the target. The magical orb I threw flew in a straight line toward the target, exploded like fireworks… and scorched the swamp as a second sun. A hot wind is blowing my way, but since I’m at a distance, I should be fine.

My older sister is staring at the flames of the Prominence I cast with a stunned expression. At this point, there’s no one else with this much power. I could take down even Takt with ease. He’s the kind of guy who’d die in a single blow. That so-called “Fake Hero,” that is.
Oh? My flames are reflected in Filo-tan’s eyes, making them sparkle. Here’s to your eyes, then. May my burning passion reach you.
“What do you think? How strong am I?”
Father, speechless, looked at the scorched wasteland that used to be the swamp, then turned his gaze back to me.
“If you like, I’ll unleash this on Melromarc Castle. It’d wipe it out in an instant, wouldn’t it?”

That would spell the end of this country. While I’m at it, I might as well turn the Church of the Three Heroes into a sea of fire and let them taste the wrath of the gods. If that’s what you want, Father, of course. Just as I was thinking this, Father turned toward me, standing tall as if he’d stretched, and asked with a proud air.
“…Stop it. It’ll be my fault again!”
Oh, it seems Father is on guard, worried he’ll be made to take the blame for everything bad that happens in Melromarc. Well, knowing those guys, there’s a good chance that’s exactly what they’ll do.
“Motoyasu.”
“Yes?”
“You said this world is just like a game, didn’t you?　What about how to enhance them? You’re sure that’s how you did it, right?”
“Are you talking about that? Of course I’ll tell you. That said, back then, I was imposing limits on my own enhancements because of my own preconceptions.”
I explained to Father, step by step, how to enhance weapons. If I can prove this is the truth, Father should believe me at least a little.
“First, the method for enhancing the Four Holy Weapons.”
“First? Does that mean there are others?”
“There are.”
“That sounds fishy.”
“You can’t do it unless you believe in it with all your heart, you know?”
“Then it’s impossible, isn’t it?”
Oh? So you don’t trust me? As I stared at him in puzzlement, Father let out another sigh.
“Sigh… Have you ever done anything to earn my trust? You’re more like an enemy, aren’t you? You’re that womanizing jerk who stabbed me with a spear just a little while ago.”

Ah, that’s right. It shouldn’t have been that long since our duel. But I can’t back down now. Drawing on the examples of my kind Father and Father from my first world, perhaps if I say the right words to persuade my current Father, he might listen.
“After all, you don’t have anything to lose, do you? I hear your future Father thought, ‘There’s nothing to lose by trusting him,’ and decided to give it a try.”
“Damn it… Stop saying things that sound like you’re reading my mind.”
Looking rather reluctant, Father began fiddling with his shield. It seems I’ve hit the nail on the head. Then Father pressed his hand to his forehead and looked down in despair.
“Um, Naofumi-sama?”
“Huh?”
“I don’t know about Weapon Copy, but I confirmed the drop. I was even able to enhance it while I was at it.”
“No way… So then…”
“It might not be a mistake, but…”
“I really wanted it to be a mistake.”
Hahaha! This is the truth! This is true love! It’s Filo-chan for love!
“So, Father, shall we destroy Melromarc?”
“…You’ve been saying nothing but that for a while now, but aren’t you just the one who wants to destroy it?”
“I don’t really feel one way or the other about it. I’ve already eliminated that scourge, the Crimson Swine, and the only thing that’s really a nuisance is the Three Heroes Sect.”

It’s a country that causes nothing but trouble, after all. It might be a good idea to show off the Hero’s strength now, wipe them out, and build your country, Father, on the remaining ruins. Just like in the first world.
“I suppose suggesting we go to Siltvelt and attack and destroy Melromarc would be another option…”
“That’s a peaceful approach.”
“What’s so peaceful about that?”

It’s peaceful enough just by leaving room for negotiation through war. Well, I wouldn’t go that far, though. I don’t want to say anything too extreme and make them wary of me even more than they already are.
“Well, since heroes are generally revered as gods to some extent, Father was in a bit of a bind with all the marriage proposals coming in.”
“Ugh… So I’m just going to be treated like a stud?”
Just as he said that, his older sister was staring at Father. The two of them gazed at each other for a while, but eventually, Father let out a deep sigh.
“Unfortunately, the answer is no. That said, to prevent another Raphtalia from emerging—and even if we resolve the wave and return to Japan—I must still fulfill my duties as a hero…”

Oh, that’s just like Father. He’s truly compassionate! To be prepared to fight after everything he’s been through—he’s a model hero. It fills me with an inexhaustible resolve to serve him for as long as I live.
“So, how do we resolve the Wave?”
“Well, actually, it should already be resolved.”
“What? What do you mean?”

“In the first world, we should have already defeated the mastermind behind the waves—the one who falsely claimed to be a god. Even in my faint memories, I clearly recall that you and the others defeated him, and peace came to the world.”
Why am I looping in the first place? The girl from the first world came to pick me up, and I should have returned, right? I don’t really understand that part either.
“I’ve been stuck in a loop before, but that was a story about a parallel world created by a spear called the ‘Minute Hand of the Dragon Hourglass’—which is different from this spear.”
I gave a rough explanation of how I’d been stuck in a loop before. Since a detailed explanation would take too long, Father just asked for the gist of it.
“A loop… huh. So, Motoyasu had been caught in a loop before, and he broke free from it, returned to the original world, took down the mastermind behind ‘The Wave,’ and brought peace to the world…”
“That’s correct.”
“So ‘The Wave’ was a man-made disaster?”
“That’s right.”
“Hmm…”
Father furrowed his brow in a troubled manner and fell deep in thought. Just like in the previous loop, perhaps I’ll get some advice this time too?
“There are several possible scenarios. The first is that, for some reason, Motoyasu’s spear malfunctioned and he wandered back into that looped world again.”
“But up until now, it always rewound immediately after summoning, didn’t it?”
“It’s a malfunction, after all… We can’t rule out the possibility that it stopped partway through. But wasn’t that spear upgraded?”
“That’s right. It’s the Minute Hand of the Dragon Hourglass.”
“In that case, the likelihood of a malfunction is low… I’m also curious about the effect of ‘parallel branching worlds.’”
Father, who had been muttering to himself as he pondered, looked up and spoke to me again.
“Another possibility is that after the so-called ‘original world’ achieved peace, some incident occurred that led to its destruction, forcing the loop to begin.”
“Is that so?”

“How would I know? Still, it’s possible, right? It’s a bit of an otaku-ish idea, but you know—like how they force a sequel to a popular anime that ended on a high note by sparking a new war in a world that had just achieved peace!”

Unfortunately, I’m not very familiar with that sort of thing, but it might be possible. After all, people fighting each other is a constant in history. But I’d hate to see a future like that. If that were actually true, we’d absolutely have to prevent it.
